title: Photography / Overview

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; visible default tab states

slide_intent: Choose a photographic approach that fits the subject so viewers can understand both the working context and the people or objects within it.
strategic_value: Editorial working-world imagery, equal-care portraiture and detailed still life can present IBM as an observant participant in real work.
demonstration: The webpage introduces IBM’s photographic point of view, then separates reportage, portraiture and still-life sections with distinct image groups.
practical_value: Choose reportage for context, portraiture for individual character or still life for objects and details instead of forcing every subject into one photographic mode.

content_islands.name: Point of view
content_islands.spec: Place the introductory rationale above a large working-space photograph and a mixed montage of people, objects and environments.

content_islands.name: Reportage: Working world
content_islands.spec: Follow the photo-types introduction with documentary scenes of work and surroundings in a compact image grid.

content_islands.name: Portraiture: Progress partners
content_islands.spec: Place the equal-care portrait rationale above photographs of individual people in varied settings.

content_islands.name: Still-life: Exhibiting excellence
content_islands.spec: End with isolated objects, arranged components and technical details on contrasting grounds, followed by page navigation.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains that photography creates context for conversations and that different subjects require different photographic approaches.
reference_purposes.Expression: The three image groups show documentary context, individual character and isolated technical objects.
reference_purposes.Application: The copy assigns reportage to the working world, portraiture to individuals and teams, and still life to objects, details and otherwise difficult-to-render concepts.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The portraiture guidance says photographic investment must not vary according to a subject’s status or stature.
